subproblem.title: Euclidean Hausdorff measure under the similarity x ↦ c + R x
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ (n = 0 allowed), let c ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) and R > 0, and put ψ(x) := c + R x. Let H^n := μHE[n] be Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Then the push-forward of H^n under ψ equals R^{-n} H^n: Measure.map ψ H^n = (ENNReal.ofReal (R^n))⁻¹ • H^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (c : Amb n ℓ) (R : ℝ), 0 < R → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).map (fun x => c + R • x) = (ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n))⁻¹ • (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+ℓ}; ψ(x) := c + R x; τ(z) := c + z; κ := (ENNReal.ofReal (R^n))⁻¹. This is step 1 of the parent proof (scaling of H^n), made precise.
1. The constant. Since R > 0 we have R^n > 0, hence ENNReal.ofReal (R^n) ∈ (0, ∞) and κ = ENNReal.ofReal ((R^n)⁻¹) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos). Moreover, as a real number ‖R⁻¹‖^n = |R⁻¹|^n = (R⁻¹)^n = (R^n)⁻¹ (Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_inv, abs_of_pos, inv_pow). Therefore the coercion of ‖R⁻¹‖₊^n ∈ ℝ≥0 to ℝ≥0∞ equals ENNReal.ofReal ((R^n)⁻¹) = κ (ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal and push_cast).
2. Preimages are dilated translates. Fix any set B ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and put T := τ⁻¹(B) = {z : c + z ∈ B}. Then ψ⁻¹(B) = R⁻¹ • T (pointwise dilation of a set): for every x, x ∈ R⁻¹ • T ⟺ R • x ∈ T (Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff₀, using R ≠ 0) ⟺ c + R x ∈ B ⟺ x ∈ ψ⁻¹(B).
3. Translation invariance. τ = IsometryEquiv.addLeft c is a surjective isometry of ℝ^{n+ℓ}. By Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_preimage, H^n(τ⁻¹(B)) = H^n(B ∩ range τ) = H^n(B ∩ univ) = H^n(B).
4. Dilation. By Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ (degree d = n, scalar r = R⁻¹ ≠ 0, set s = T): H^n(R⁻¹ • T) = ‖R⁻¹‖₊^n • H^n(T). Combining steps 1–3: H^n(ψ⁻¹(B)) = H^n(R⁻¹ • T) = κ · H^n(T) = κ · H^n(B). This holds for every set B (no measurability needed).
5. Equality of measures. ψ is continuous, hence Borel measurable. For every measurable B, (Measure.map ψ H^n)(B) = H^n(ψ⁻¹(B)) (Measure.map_apply) = κ · H^n(B) (step 4) = (κ • H^n)(B) (Measure.smul_apply). Two measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext), so Measure.map ψ H^n = κ • H^n = (ENNReal.ofReal (R^n))⁻¹ • H^n. Nothing in the argument uses n ≥ 1.
6. Implementation note: the pointwise set dilation R⁻¹ • T used in steps 2 and 4 needs `open scoped Pointwise` in Lean (add it locally, e.g. `open scoped Pointwise in` before the theorem); the frozen statement itself does not use pointwise notation.

ψ⁻¹(B) = R⁻¹ • (c + ·)⁻¹(B) for every set B
μHE[n] is invariant under the surjective isometry z ↦ c + z
Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ with r = R⁻¹ gives H^n(ψ⁻¹B) = κ H^n(B)

subproblem.title: Generalized mean curvature of the rescaled varifold
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} be any set, let V be a rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight μ_V, let c ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, R > 0, ψ(x) := c + R x and φ(y) := R⁻¹(y − c), and let W be a rectifiable n-varifold in ψ⁻¹(U) with W.weight = (ENNReal.ofReal (R^n))⁻¹ • Measure.map φ μ_V and W.tangentProj(x) = V.tangentProj(c + R x) for every x. Let H : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Suppose V has generalized mean curvature H in U (contract HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature): H is locally μ_V-integrable on U (LocallyIntegrableOn H U μ_V), and ∫ div_V X dμ_V = −∫ ⟨X, H⟩ dμ_V for every C¹ map X : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ} with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U, where div_V X(x) = trace(DX(x) ∘ V.tangentProj(x)). Then W has generalized mean curvature H'(x) := R H(c + R x) in ψ⁻¹(U) (with div_W built from W.tangentProj and integrals against W.weight). All integrals are Mathlib Bochner integrals, which are 0 for non-integrable integrands.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (c : Amb n ℓ) (R : ℝ), 0 < R → ∀ W : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ ((fun x => c + R • x) ⁻¹' U), W.weight = (ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n))⁻¹ • V.weight.map (fun x => R⁻¹ • (x - c)) → (∀ x, W.tangentProj x = V.tangentProj (c + R • x)) → ∀ H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ, V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → W.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature (fun x => R • H (c + R • x))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)); H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^{n+ℓ}; for c ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and R > 0, ψ(x) := c + R x and φ(y) := R⁻¹(y − c); κ := (ENNReal.ofReal (R^n))⁻¹, i.e. R^{-n} as an element of [0, ∞]. Write μ_W := W.weight and H'(x) := R H(c + R x). This is step 6 of the parent proof.
1. Maps and constant. κ ≠ ∞ because ENNReal.ofReal (R^n) > 0. Let e be the homeomorphism x ↦ c + R x (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero R followed by Homeomorph.addLeft c). Since ψ(φ(y)) = c + R R⁻¹ (y − c) = y, injectivity of e gives e⁻¹ = φ. Hence φ is a homeomorphism and a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding), ψ(φ(y)) = y and φ(ψ(x)) = x.
2. Integral formula: for every g : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ, ∫ g dμ_W = κ.toReal · ∫ g(φ(y)) dμ_V(y). Indeed integral_smul_measure gives ∫ g d(κ • ν) = κ.toReal • ∫ g dν for every g, and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map gives ∫ g d(Measure.map φ μ_V) = ∫ g ∘ φ dμ_V for every g. Neither identity needs integrability, so the Bochner integrals correspond also when they vanish by non-integrability; no case split is needed.
3. Integrability transfer: for every set S and g : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ}, if g ∘ φ is μ_V-integrable on φ⁻¹(S), then g is μ_W-integrable on S. Indeed IntegrableOn g S (Measure.map φ μ_V) ⟺ IntegrableOn (g ∘ φ) (φ⁻¹(S)) μ_V (MeasurableEmbedding.integrableOn_map_iff), and since (κ • ν)⌞S = κ • (ν⌞S) (Measure.restrict_smul), integrability for ν⌞S passes to κ • (ν⌞S) because κ ≠ ∞ (Integrable.smul_measure).
4. Local integrability of H' on ψ⁻¹(U). LocallyIntegrableOn f s μ means: for every x ∈ s there is t ∈ 𝓝[s] x such that f is μ-integrable on t. Let x ∈ ψ⁻¹(U); then ψ(x) ∈ U. By the first half of V's hypothesis there is t ∈ 𝓝[U] ψ(x) with H μ_V-integrable on t. ψ is continuous and maps ψ⁻¹(U) into U, so ψ tends from 𝓝[ψ⁻¹(U)] x to 𝓝[U] ψ(x) (ContinuousWithinAt.tendsto_nhdsWithin with MapsTo from mapsTo_preimage). Hence ψ⁻¹(t) ∈ 𝓝[ψ⁻¹(U)] x. Moreover φ⁻¹(ψ⁻¹(t)) = t (since ψ ∘ φ = id), and H' ∘ φ = (y ↦ R H(ψ(φ(y)))) = R H, which is μ_V-integrable on t as a constant multiple of H (Integrable.smul). By step 3 with S := ψ⁻¹(t), H' is μ_W-integrable on ψ⁻¹(t). So H' is locally μ_W-integrable on ψ⁻¹(U). This is the parent's change-of-variables argument for local integrability, applied to a relative neighbourhood instead of a compact set, so no openness of U is needed.
5. Transported test field. Let X' : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ} be C¹ with compact support and tsupport X' ⊆ ψ⁻¹(U). Define X(y) := R X'(φ(y)).
(a) X is C¹: φ is affine, hence C^∞; so X' ∘ φ is C¹ (ContDiff.comp), and so is its constant multiple (ContDiff.const_smul).
(b) X has compact support: X = (v ↦ R v) ∘ X' ∘ e⁻¹; X' ∘ e⁻¹ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph), and left composition with a map sending 0 to 0 preserves compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left, R · 0 = 0).
(c) tsupport X ⊆ U: since R ≠ 0, X(y) ≠ 0 ⟺ X'(φ(y)) ≠ 0, so support X = φ⁻¹(support X'). As φ = e⁻¹ is a homeomorphism, closure(φ⁻¹(support X')) = φ⁻¹(closure(support X')) (Homeomorph.preimage_closure), i.e. tsupport X = φ⁻¹(tsupport X'). If y ∈ tsupport X, then φ(y) ∈ tsupport X' ⊆ ψ⁻¹(U), so y = ψ(φ(y)) ∈ U.
(d) By the second half of V's hypothesis, ∫ div_V X dμ_V = −∫ ⟨X(y), H(y)⟩ dμ_V(y).
6. Derivative: for every y, DX(y) = DX'(φ(y)). X' is differentiable at φ(y) with derivative L := DX'(φ(y)) (C¹ with 1 ≠ 0 implies differentiable). φ has derivative R⁻¹ · id at y (derivative of y ↦ y − c is the identity; HasFDerivAt.sub_const and HasFDerivAt.const_smul). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp) and the constant-multiple rule, X has derivative R · (L ∘ (R⁻¹ · id)) at y. For every v, R · L(R⁻¹ v) = R R⁻¹ L(v) = L(v) by linearity, so this derivative is L. Uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative (HasFDerivAt.fderiv) gives DX(y) = L.
7. Divergence identity: for every y, div_W X'(φ(y)) = trace(DX'(φ(y)) ∘ W.tangentProj(φ(y))) = trace(DX'(φ(y)) ∘ V.tangentProj(ψ(φ(y)))) (hypothesis on tangentProj) = trace(DX(y) ∘ V.tangentProj(y)) (ψ(φ(y)) = y and step 6) = div_V X(y).
8. Pairing identity: for every y, ⟨X'(φ(y)), H'(φ(y))⟩ = ⟨X'(φ(y)), R H(ψ(φ(y)))⟩ = ⟨X'(φ(y)), R H(y)⟩ = R ⟨X'(φ(y)), H(y)⟩ = ⟨R X'(φ(y)), H(y)⟩ = ⟨X(y), H(y)⟩ (inner_smul_right, real_inner_smul_left).
9. First variation of W. ∫ div_W X' dμ_W = κ.toReal · ∫ div_W X'(φ(y)) dμ_V(y) (step 2) = κ.toReal · ∫ div_V X dμ_V (step 7) = κ.toReal · (−∫ ⟨X, H⟩ dμ_V) (step 5(d)) = −κ.toReal · ∫ ⟨X'(φ(y)), H'(φ(y))⟩ dμ_V(y) (step 8) = −∫ ⟨X'(x), H'(x)⟩ dμ_W(x) (step 2 again, mul_neg).
10. Steps 4 and 9 are the two clauses of W.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H'. Hence W has generalized mean curvature x ↦ R H(c + R x) in ψ⁻¹(U).
proof_key_steps: φ = e⁻¹ is a homeomorphism; ∫ g dμ_W = κ.toReal ∫ g∘φ dμ_V for every g (integral_smul_measure, integral_map)
local integrability of R H∘ψ via relative neighbourhoods ψ⁻¹(t) and integrableOn_map_iff
test field X = R X'∘φ is C¹, compactly supported, with tsupport X = φ⁻¹(tsupport X') ⊆ U
chain rule DX(y) = DX'(φ y); with the tangentProj hypothesis div_W X'(φ y) = div_V X(y)
pairing ⟨X'∘φ, H'∘φ⟩ = ⟨X, H⟩ and transfer of the first-variation identity

subproblem.title: Support of the rescaled varifold

(⊆) Let z ∈ ψ⁻¹(M) and w = r⁻¹(z − x). Put m := ψ(z) ∈ M. Then m − p = (c + R z) − (c + R x) = R(z − x), so η_{p,R r}(m) = (R r)⁻¹ R (z − x) = R⁻¹ r⁻¹ R (z − x) = r⁻¹ (z − x) = w.
(⊇) Let m ∈ M and w = (R r)⁻¹(m − p). Put z := R⁻¹(m − c). Then ψ(z) = c + R R⁻¹ (m − c) = m ∈ M, so z ∈ ψ⁻¹(M); and z − x = R⁻¹(m − c) − R⁻¹ R x = R⁻¹(m − p), so η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹ R⁻¹ (m − p) = (R r)⁻¹ (m − p) = w.

For equal predicates q₁ = q₂ and any proofs h₁ : ∃P, q₁ P and h₂ : ∃P, q₂ P, Classical.choose h₁ = Classical.choose h₂ (substitute q₂ := q₁; the proofs of the same proposition are equal by proof irrelevance). subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} be any set, and let V = v(M, θ) be a rectifiable n-varifold in U in the sense of the frozen contract (structure RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U): M ⊆ U is H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable (M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with H^n(M₀) = 0 and each F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^{n+ℓ} Lipschitz), and θ : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ is positive on M, almost-everywhere measurable for H^n⌞M, and H^n-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U, where H^n = μHE[n]. 1. ψ is a homeomorphism. ψ is the composite of the homeomorphisms x ↦ R x (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero R, R ≠ 0) and z ↦ c + z (Homeomorph.addLeft c); its inverse is φ, since ψ(φ(y)) = c + R R⁻¹ (y − c) = y and φ(ψ(x)) = R⁻¹ (c + R x − c) = x. Hence ψ is continuous, injective and a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding). Also κ ≠ ∞, because ENNReal.ofReal (R^n) > 0 (R^n > 0).
2. Measure-theoretic consequences of the sibling lemma map_hausdorff, which gives Measure.map ψ H^n = κ • H^n. (a) For every set B: H^n(ψ⁻¹(B)) = (Measure.map ψ H^n)(B) (MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply, valid for every set) = κ · H^n(B); in particular H^n(B) = 0 implies H^n(ψ⁻¹(B)) = 0. (b) ψ is quasi-measure-preserving from H^n to H^n: ψ is measurable and Measure.map ψ H^n = κ • H^n ≪ H^n (Measure.smul_absolutelyContinuous).

(i) carrier_subset: M ⊆ U gives ψ⁻¹(M) ⊆ ψ⁻¹(U) (preimage_mono).
(ii) nullMeasurableSet_carrier: M is H^n-null-measurable and ψ is quasi-measure-preserving (2b), so ψ⁻¹(M) is H^n-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.preimage).
(iii) countablyRectifiable: take M₀ and F_j from the countable rectifiability of M. Put M₀' := ψ⁻¹(M₀), which is H^n-null by 2(a), and F_j'(z) := R⁻¹ (F_j(z) − c) = φ(F_j(z)). If F_j is K_j-Lipschitz, then z ↦ F_j(z) − c is (K_j + 0)-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.sub with the 0-Lipschitz constant map) and v ↦ R⁻¹ v is ‖R⁻¹‖₊-Lipschitz (lipschitzWith_smul), so F_j' is (‖R⁻¹‖₊ · (K_j + 0))-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp). Covering: let x ∈ ψ⁻¹(M), so ψ(x) ∈ M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j. If ψ(x) ∈ M₀ then x ∈ M₀'. Otherwise ψ(x) = F_j(z) for some j and z, and then F_j'(z) = R⁻¹ (c + R x − c) = R⁻¹ R x = x, so x ∈ range F_j'. Hence ψ⁻¹(M) ⊆ M₀' ∪ ⋃_j range F_j'.

(v) aemeasurable_mult: by MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, Measure.map ψ (H^n⌞ψ⁻¹(M)) = (Measure.map ψ H^n)⌞M = (κ • H^n)⌞M = κ • (H^n⌞M) (Measure.restrict_smul). θ is a.e.-measurable for H^n⌞M, hence for κ • (H^n⌞M) (AEMeasurable.smul_measure), i.e. for Measure.map ψ (H^n⌞ψ⁻¹(M)). subproblem.title: Weight of the rescaled varifold
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, let U, U' ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} be arbitrary sets, let V be a rectifiable n-varifold in U with carrier M, multiplicity θ and weight μ_V = (H^n⌞M).withDensity (ofReal ∘ θ), and let W be a rectifiable n-varifold in U' with weight μ_W = (H^n⌞W.carrier).withDensity (ofReal ∘ W.mult), where H^n = μHE[n]. Let c ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, R > 0, ψ(x) := c + R x and φ(y) := R⁻¹(y − c). If W.carrier = ψ⁻¹(M) and W.mult(x) = θ(c + R x) for every x, then μ_W = R^{-n} φ_# μ_V, i.e. W.weight = (ENNReal.ofReal (R^n))⁻¹ • Measure.map φ V.weight.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U U' : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (W : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U') (c : Amb n ℓ) (R : ℝ), 0 < R → W.carrier = (fun x => c + R • x) ⁻¹' V.carrier → (∀ x, W.mult x = V.mult (c + R • x)) → W.weight = (ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n))⁻¹ • V.weight.map (fun x => R⁻¹ • (x - c))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)); H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^{n+ℓ}; for c ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and R > 0, ψ(x) := c + R x and φ(y) := R⁻¹(y − c); κ := (ENNReal.ofReal (R^n))⁻¹, i.e. R^{-n} as an element of [0, ∞]. This is step 3 of the parent proof.
1. Maps. ψ is a homeomorphism (x ↦ R x via Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero R, then z ↦ c + z via Homeomorph.addLeft c), hence a measurable embedding. φ is continuous, hence measurable. For every x, φ(ψ(x)) = R⁻¹ (c + R x − c) = R⁻¹ R x = x.
2. Change of variables. For every set S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and every g : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → [0, ∞]: ∫⁻_{ψ⁻¹(S)} g(ψ(x)) dH^n(x) = κ · ∫⁻_S g dH^n. Proof: by MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, (Measure.map ψ H^n)⌞S = Measure.map ψ (H^n⌞ψ⁻¹(S)), and by MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map, ∫⁻ g d(Measure.map ψ (H^n⌞ψ⁻¹(S))) = ∫⁻_{ψ⁻¹(S)} g ∘ ψ dH^n. On the other hand the sibling lemma map_hausdorff gives Measure.map ψ H^n = κ • H^n, so (Measure.map ψ H^n)⌞S = κ • (H^n⌞S) (Measure.restrict_smul) and ∫⁻ g d(κ • (H^n⌞S)) = κ · ∫⁻_S g dH^n (lintegral_smul_measure).
3. Left side on a measurable set. Fix a measurable set A. By withDensity_apply (A measurable) and Measure.restrict_restrict (A measurable): W.weight(A) = ∫⁻_{A ∩ W.carrier} ofReal(W.mult(x)) dH^n(x).
4. Right side on A. φ⁻¹(A) is measurable. By Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply (φ measurable, A measurable): (κ • Measure.map φ V.weight)(A) = κ · V.weight(φ⁻¹(A)) = κ · ∫⁻_{φ⁻¹(A) ∩ M} ofReal(θ(y)) dH^n(y) (withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict for the measurable set φ⁻¹(A)).
5. Set identity. A ∩ W.carrier = ψ⁻¹(φ⁻¹(A) ∩ M): indeed W.carrier = ψ⁻¹(M), ψ⁻¹(φ⁻¹(A)) = (φ ∘ ψ)⁻¹(A) = A by step 1, and preimages commute with intersections (preimage_inter). Also ofReal(W.mult(x)) = ofReal(θ(ψ(x))) for every x.
6. Conclusion on A. W.weight(A) = ∫⁻_{ψ⁻¹(φ⁻¹(A) ∩ M)} ofReal(θ(ψ(x))) dH^n(x) = κ · ∫⁻_{φ⁻¹(A) ∩ M} ofReal(θ(y)) dH^n(y) (step 2 with S := φ⁻¹(A) ∩ M and g := ofReal ∘ θ) = (κ • Measure.map φ V.weight)(A) (step 4).
7. Two measures that agree on every measurable set are equal (Measure.ext). Hence W.weight = (ENNReal.ofReal (R^n))⁻¹ • Measure.map φ V.weight.
